chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding the prayer in Mecca, he said: 'Whoever wishes may complete (the prayer) and whoever wishes may shorten (it).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for shortening prayer in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique status of Mecca as a place of residence (*watan*) for all Muslims, granting them the flexibility to choose between *qasr* (shortening) and *tamam* (completing) their prayers. This ruling distinguishes Mecca from other travel destinations, reflecting the scholarly consensus that the traveler's privilege to shorten prayers does not apply within the holy city itself, yet the option to perform the full four-rak'ah prayer remains available as a concession.
